summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR 767 million, with EBITDA margin steady at 21.1% and PAT up 54.8% to INR 113 million.
summary.overview: Mobavenue reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 767 million, up 41.3% YoY and 5.4% QoQ, with H1 revenue of INR 1,496 million up 48.6%. Gross margin widened to 41.5% as supply-end data cost fell to 58.5% of revenue from 61.5% a year ago. EBITDA was INR 660 million at a 21.1% margin, and PAT was INR 113 million at a 14.7% margin. Employee costs rose 62.3% YoY as the company invested ahead of growth, while international revenue share doubled to 23.8%.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Remains the primary market and the base for technology and operations; India RPO is lower than international markets but was lifted by premiumisation into OTT, DOOH and Apple inventory. Management did not disclose a segment revenue split.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Contributed 23.8% of Q2 FY27 revenue versus 12.3% a year ago. Singapore is the Southeast Asia hub; the US subsidiary is being set up for direct clients and UK, Latin America and Middle East are also active.

segments.name: Channel mix
segments.commentary: Direct clients contributed 64.7% of Q2 FY27 revenue; agencies, mid and small agencies, Holdco, resellers and partners contributed 35.3%.

segments.name: PiiX (Apple Ads platform)
segments.commentary: Launched about 5 months ago; currently not a material revenue contributor per management, which is focused on adoption and advertiser onboarding.

guidance_outlook: Long-term 'rule of 50' framework: revenue growth above 30% a year with EBITDA margin of 20% or above; management said H1 growth of about 49% at 21% EBITDA exceeds this.
Management did not set a numeric target but said it is confident of the next half, citing Q3 festive demand in India and the Q4 year-end spend in global markets.
Direct-client share is expected to rise over the medium to long term as international reseller-led entry shifts toward direct clients.
Expected 2030 vision built around growth with profitability; no specific FY27 revenue or margin guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model; management said scaling needs limited incremental infrastructure investment.
Platform processes about 1.4 billion signals a day, reaches about 2.7 billion devices globally and makes decisions in under 15 milliseconds.
Mobavenue Neural Engine, launched earlier in 2026, is in production with four capabilities: planning, execution, creative intelligence and conversational reporting.
Merger of the wholly owned Indian subsidiary into Mobavenue AI Tech Ltd initiated to consolidate Indian operations.
Headcount and talent investment was made to add capacity ahead of growth, including global teams and technology.
demand_pricing: Client base of about 170 brands across 13 countries; verticals include Quick Commerce, BFSI, Fintech, Super Apps, entertainment, travel and commerce.
RPO (revenue per outcome) rose about 10% YoY to INR 50.67 in Q2 FY27, which management attributed to premium inventory (OTT, DOOH, Apple) and better models.
In India, Mobavenue holds about 3-4% of a client's marketing spend and targets 7-10% of alternate-platform spend (up to 10-25% in some cases); it is typically a top-two or top-three partner.
Onboarding takes under 3-5 days after agreement, with results in 2-3 weeks; management says share of wallet typically grows within 2-3 months.
Chatbot and LLM ad inventory is currently closed and search-led; management said it is in process of integrating these systems into its platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Given ~INR 220 crore FY26 revenue and INR 145 crore in H1, how confident is management of 30% growth and a 20% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth of about 49% at 21% EBITDA exceeds the 30% framework; RPO up about 10% to INR 50.67 and international share at 23.8% support confidence. No numeric target was set.

qa_highlights.question: What drove EBITDA margin above 20% for three consecutive quarters and what is the medium-term outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an outcome-based revenue model, an asset-light cost structure and operating leverage as revenue grows faster than costs. It reiterated the rule-of-50 framework.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international vs India RPO difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give ranges; it said emerging markets have slightly higher RPO than India and the US and UK are higher still, and that the blended figure is used in modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Is PiiX generating revenue and how is it performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue contribution was not quantified; PiiX was launched about 5 months ago and is being used as a utility to speed advertiser onboarding. Management expects revenue to build over time, with advertiser adds as the year-end metric.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the direct-client share decline, and what is the channel mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied a relative decline, citing agency and reseller routes for entry into emerging markets. It is hiring direct teams and expects the direct share to rise over the medium to long term.

qa_highlights.question: Can Mobavenue serve ads on chatbots and LLM platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Current chatbot ad systems are closed and search-intent driven. Mobavenue is integrating them and expects to access them as they open up to programmatic exchanges.

risks_watch: Employee costs grew 62.3% YoY, far above revenue growth, so margin depends on revenue keeping pace with the capacity added ahead of growth.
Direct-client share is falling as a share of revenue during international expansion; management aims to reverse this, so track the direct versus agency mix next quarter.
PiiX revenue contribution is undisclosed and early; watch advertiser onboarding numbers at year-end.
Q2 EBITDA and PAT were flat QoQ at about INR 113 million PAT, so sequential momentum is limited.
Reliance on the outcome-based model and on platform-level pricing (RPO) with no disclosed range by geography; the metric is not yet broken out by region.
Chatbot ad inventory access is a future opportunity but not yet available.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with management stating it is pretty confident of the next half. It was evasive on specifics: no RPO ranges by geography, no PiiX revenue, and no numeric FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 was another quarter of profitable scale for Mobavenue.

We have repeatedly mentioned that our long-term philosophy is guided by the rule of 50, which means sustaining the annual revenue growth of more than 30% while maintaining EBITDA margins of 20% or above.
We are not looking today, from a revenue perspective, how much today it will start contributing.

growth.why: Management reiterated a long-term rule of 50 (over 30% revenue growth, EBITDA margin of 20%+) but gave no numeric FY27 guidance; confidence in the next half rests on Q3 festive demand and Q4 global spend, with no specific capacity or contracts quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin held at 21.1% (about 80 bps up YoY from 20.3%) and gross margin widened to 41.5% as data cost fell to 58.5% of revenue from 61.5%, though employee costs up 62.3% YoY cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management calls the model asset-light with limited incremental infrastructure needed, and capacity was added through headcount ahead of growth rather than plants, so no new physical capacity is expected.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 48.6% to INR 1,496 million and management is confident of the next half on Q3 festive demand and Q4 global spend, with RPO up about 10% to INR 50.67.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and the asset-light model means limited infrastructure spend; utilisation was not disclosed, so there is no basis for a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, but H1 growth of about 49% with 21% EBITDA already exceeds its 30%/20% rule-of-50 framework, so a formal raise is possible if H2 holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Employee costs up 62.3% YoY far outpace revenue growth and PAT was flat QoQ at about INR 113 million, so margin could compress if revenue slows from the 41% YoY pace.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PiiX (launched about 5 months ago) is not yet material, and chatbot/LLM ad inventory is being integrated but is closed today, so new revenue streams depend on platform access.

rows.label: International expansion (US subsidiary, UK, LatAm, Middle East)
rows.why: International share rose to 23.8% of Q2 revenue from 12.3% a year ago, with the US subsidiary being set up for direct clients and several regions already active.

rows.label: Merger of Indian subsidiary into parent
rows.why: Management has initiated the merger of the wholly owned Indian subsidiary into Mobavenue AI Tech Ltd to consolidate Indian operations.

rows.label: Direct-client share reversal
rows.why: Direct clients were 64.7% of Q2 revenue and management expects the direct share to rise over the medium to long term, but it is hiring direct teams with no quantified target.

tone.note: Management was confident on the rule-of-50 framework and the next half (Q3 festive, Q4 global spend) but evasive on RPO by geography, PiiX revenue and numeric FY27 guidance; analysts probed whether 30% growth and 20% margin were sustainable given the 62% rise in employee costs.
